question: Can a black hole suck up the entire Universe?
short_answer: No. A black hole's gravity follows the inverse-square law, pulling objects no more than any normal star or planet of the same mass at a given distance.
full_explanation: If the Sun were replaced by a 1-solar-mass black hole, Earth would continue in its current orbit without falling in, though the planet would freeze from lack of sunlight.
